meta.audience: The people of Zarahemla, from the city wall
meta.location: The wall of the city of Zarahemla
principles: Signs given with a date attached
A death that produces a resurrection
Freedom stated as the ground of judgment

world_behind.title: The prophecy is dated
world_behind.text: Verse 2 says five years, and 3 Nephi 1 reports the fulfillment in the ninety-second year.

world_behind.title: Two sets of signs are given
world_behind.text: Verses 3 through 6 cover the birth and verses 20 through 25 the death. 3 Nephi 1 reports the first set arriving and 3 Nephi 8 the second, so one chapter of prophecy is checked against two chapters of narrative thirty-three years apart.

world_behind.title: The birth sign is a night without darkness
world_behind.text: Verse 4 describes a day, a night, and a day running together while the sun keeps its ordinary rising and setting. 3 Nephi 1:15 and 19 report exactly that five years later, including the sun rising in the morning according to its proper order, so the prediction and the fulfilment can be laid side by side.

world_behind.title: A new star is promised
world_behind.text: Verse 5 says one never before seen, and 3 Nephi 1:21 reports that it appeared.

world_behind.title: Samuel names his own position
world_behind.text: Verse 10 says he is a Lamanite, that the message was hard against them, and that they had cast him out. Helaman 13:2 records that expulsion, and Helaman 16:7 has him climb down the wall and go home to his own country, never heard of again among the Nephites.

world_behind.title: The death signs are geological
world_behind.text: Verses 21 through 24 describe solid rock broken into seams and cracks, mountains and valleys trading places, and highways broken up. 3 Nephi 8:13 and 18 report the same three things in the same order thirty-three years later, using the phrase "seams and cracks" that occurs in scripture only in these two places.

world_behind.title: The chapter closes on agency
world_behind.text: Verses 30 and 31 say they are free, permitted to act for themselves, and given knowledge to choose with. 2 Nephi 2:27 and Alma 12:31 put the same claim at the two other places the record stops to argue for agency, so this closing is the third statement of a settled Nephite doctrine rather than a new one.

words.text: A luminous body in the night sky. The record uses the singular twice, here and at 3 Nephi 1:21, where the promised one appears. The King James Bible has it fifteen times, including the star seen in the east.
Treated at 2 Nephi 31:19, of relying wholly on the merits of Christ. The record uses the word five times and the King James Bible never. Verse 13 makes remission come through them.
Is necessary or fitting for. It appears four times in the record, and the King James Bible never. Verse 15 pairs it with "becometh expedient" about the death of Christ.
Lines along which broken pieces meet. Both of the record's uses are of this one event, in the prophecy here and in the report at 3 Nephi 8:18. The King James Bible has neither this word nor "cracks."
Violent storms. The record uses the word fifteen times and the King James Bible twenty-two. Verse 23 places tempests alongside mountains laid low and valleys raised.
Burial places. The record uses the plural three times, twice in Ether 6 of Jaredite burials and once here. Verse 25 has them opening and yielding up their dead.

phrases.term: For five years more cometh, and behold, then cometh the Son of God
phrases.text: A prophecy with a countdown attached. Samuel makes the claim checkable inside the lifetime of everyone hearing it.

phrases.term: In the night before he cometh there shall be no darkness
phrases.text: The sign that would be impossible to miss and impossible to stage. Verse 4 spells out how it will look from the ground.

phrases.term: There shall a new star arise, such an one as ye never have beheld
phrases.text: A second sign, given without explanation. 3 Nephi 1:21 reports it in one sentence when it happens.

phrases.term: Because I am a Lamanite, and have spoken unto you the words which the Lord hath commanded me
phrases.text: Samuel naming both reasons they are angry. His nation and his message are given as the causes, in that order.

phrases.term: For this intent have I come up upon the walls of this city
phrases.text: The purpose of the wall. He lists three things they might know: the judgments, the terms of repentance, and Christ's coming.

phrases.term: That thereby ye may have a remission of them through his merits
phrases.text: The mechanism stated in a clause. Belief leads to repentance, and repentance to remission through what belongs to Christ.

phrases.term: He surely must die that salvation may come
phrases.text: The necessity stated plainly. Verse 15 gives the purpose as the resurrection of the dead and the return to God's presence.

phrases.term: The resurrection of Christ redeemeth mankind, yea, even all mankind
phrases.text: The universal claim. Verse 18 immediately distinguishes what happens after that return, and names a second death.

phrases.term: They shall be rent in twain, and shall ever after be found in seams and in cracks
phrases.text: A prophecy about the future condition of rock. The phrase "ever after" makes it a permanent feature of the land.

phrases.term: Many graves shall be opened, and shall yield up many of their dead
phrases.text: The sign 3 Nephi 23:11 will have Christ asking why nobody wrote down. Samuel gives it here five years before the birth.

phrases.term: Ye are free; ye are permitted to act for yourselves
phrases.text: The ground of everything the chapter has said. Verse 31 adds the knowledge that makes the freedom usable.

verses.label: v. 3–5
verses.title: A sign made testable by being described as unprecedented
verses.text: The record specifies the first sign in a way that rules out ordinary weather: "there shall be great lights in heaven, insomuch that in the night before he cometh there shall be no darkness," and "there shall be one day and a night and a day, as if it were one day and there were no night." Then verse 5 adds a second item and stakes it on novelty: "there shall a new star arise, such an one as ye never have beheld." A witness who had seen the star before would falsify it.

verses.label: v. 9–11
verses.title: The speaker names his own disadvantage
verses.text: The record has Samuel say why he expects to be disbelieved before he asks to be heard: "because I am a Lamanite, and have spoken unto you the words which the Lord hath commanded me, and because it was hard against you, ye are angry with me." Verse 11 states the practical reason for the position he is speaking from: "for this intent have I come up upon the walls of this city, that ye might hear and know of the judgments of God." The wall and the nationality are both stated as obstacles rather than as credentials.

verses.label: v. 30–31
verses.title: A chapter of fixed signs closes on choice
verses.text: The last two verses turn from what will happen to what is up to the hearer, and say it twice: "whosoever perisheth, perisheth unto himself; and whosoever doeth iniquity, doeth it unto himself." Verse 31 states the equipment given: "he hath given unto you that ye might know good from evil, and he hath given unto you that ye might choose life or death." Everything before this point is a schedule of events nobody in the chapter can alter. The last thing said is that the outcome is nevertheless theirs.

chapter.title: The prophecy carries a deadline
chapter.text: Five years is short enough that the audience will see the outcome. Samuel gives a sign that will either arrive on schedule or discredit him.

chapter.title: Both signs are public and physical
chapter.text: A night without darkness, a new star, three days of darkness, rock broken into seams. Nothing depends on private experience.

chapter.title: He explains why he is unwelcome before continuing
chapter.text: Verse 10 names his nationality and the hardness of the message. He does not soften either one.

chapter.title: The wall is given a purpose
chapter.text: Verse 11 says he came up there so they could hear. The improvisation of Helaman 13:4 is now stated as intent.

chapter.title: The resurrection is universal and the second death is not
chapter.text: Verses 17 and 18 hold both: all mankind brought back, and those who do not repent cut off again.

chapter.title: The geology is specific and permanent
chapter.text: Verse 22 says the rocks will be found in seams and cracks "ever after." 3 Nephi 8:18 uses the same two words in the report.

chapter.title: One sign went unrecorded
chapter.text: Verse 25 promises graves opened and saints appearing, and 3 Nephi 23:11 has Christ asking why it was not written down.

chapter.title: Agency is the closing argument
chapter.text: Verse 30 states the principle twice in one sentence, "whosoever perisheth, perisheth unto himself; and whosoever doeth iniquity, doeth it unto himself," and gives the ground, "ye are free; ye are permitted to act for yourselves." Verse 31 supplies the two gifts that make the freedom operative, knowledge of good and evil and the power to choose "life or death." Verse 29 has already stated the purpose of all the preceding signs in the same terms, "if they are condemned they bring upon themselves their own condemnation." Thirty verses of dated predictions close on a claim about who is responsible for the outcome.

applications.title: Attach a date when you can
applications.text: Five years made the claim testable. A prediction with a deadline is a different kind of statement from one without.

applications.title: Make the sign specific enough to fail
applications.text: Samuel does not simply promise a bright night; he says the rising and the setting will still be known, so that it counts as two days and a night with no darkness between. A prediction detailed enough to be recognized is detailed enough to be wrong, which is what makes it worth anything.

applications.title: Say why you are hard to hear
applications.text: He named his nationality and his message as the two reasons they were angry. Acknowledging the obstacle is not the same as apologizing for the message.

applications.title: State the purpose of the odd method
applications.text: He explained the wall. When you do something unusual to be heard, saying why keeps it from looking like a stunt.

applications.title: Explain the mechanism, not only the event
applications.text: Samuel does not just predict a death; he says what it accomplishes, that the resurrection redeems mankind and brings them back into the presence of the Lord. When you deliver a hard fact, the reason it is necessary is part of the delivery.

applications.title: Knowing is itself an obligation
applications.text: The warning is against coming under condemnation by knowing these things and not doing them. Learning something raises the standard you are held to, so treat the learning as having taken on a debt.

applications.title: Repeat the attribution as the claim grows
applications.text: As the predictions get larger, Samuel twice restates that this is what the angel said to him. The bigger the claim, the more useful it is to keep naming where it came from.

applications.title: Treat freedom as the reason it matters
applications.text: Samuel ends on the fact that they can act. Knowing you could have done otherwise is what makes any of the rest weigh anything.

questions.text: What am I willing to predict with a date on it?
What sign would I actually accept?
What about me makes my message harder for people to receive?
What do I think a remission of sins rests on?
What do I know and not do?
What has happened to me that I never wrote down?
Where am I acting as though I had no choice?

entries.head: Hel. 13:2

anchor.quote: because I am a Lamanite, and have spoken unto you the words which the Lord hath commanded me

entries.reason: the arrival and the casting out that preceded the wall

targets.quote: he did preach, many days, repentance unto the people, and they did cast him out,
targets.verse_text: And it came to pass that in this year there was one Samuel, a Lamanite, came into the land of Zarahemla, and began to preach unto the people. And it came to pass that he did preach, many days, repentance unto the people, and they did cast him out, and he was about to return to his own land.
targets.markdown: And it came to pass that in this year there was one Samuel, a Lamanite, came into the land of Zarahemla, and began to preach unto the people. And it came to pass that **he did preach, many days, repentance unto the people, and they did cast him out**, and he was about to return to his own land.

entries.head: Hel. 16:1

anchor.quote: whosoever will believe might be saved

entries.reason: the ones who did believe, and what they did next

targets.quote: as many as believed on his word went forth and sought for Nephi;
targets.verse_text: And now, it came to pass that there were many who heard the words of Samuel, the Lamanite, which he spake upon the walls of the city. And as many as believed on his word went forth and sought for Nephi; and when they had come forth and found him they confessed unto him their sins and denied not, desiring that they might be baptized unto the Lord.
targets.markdown: And now, it came to pass that there were many who heard the words of Samuel, the Lamanite, which he spake upon the walls of the city. And **as many as believed on his word went forth and sought for Nephi**; and when they had come forth and found him they confessed unto him their sins and denied not, desiring that they might be baptized unto the Lord.

entries.head: 2 Ne. 2:27

entries.reason: Lehi putting the same freedom as a choice of ends

targets.verse_text: Wherefore, men are free according to the flesh; and all things are given them which are expedient unto man. And they are free to choose liberty and eternal life, through the great Mediator of all men, or to choose captivity and death, according to the captivity and power of the devil; for he seeketh that all men might be miserable like unto himself.
targets.markdown: Wherefore, men are free according to the flesh; and all things are given them which are expedient unto man. And **they are free to choose liberty and eternal life**, through the great Mediator of all men, or to choose captivity and death, according to the captivity and power of the devil; for he seeketh that all men might be miserable like unto himself.

And because that they are redeemed from the fall they have become free forever, knowing good from evil; to act for themselves and not to be acted upon, save it be by the punishment of the law at the great and last day, according to the commandments which God hath given.
targets.markdown: And the Messiah cometh in the fulness of time, that he may redeem the children of men from the fall. And because that they are redeemed from the fall they have become free forever, knowing good from evil; **to act for themselves and not to be acted upon**, save it be by the punishment of the law at the great and last day, according to the commandments which God hath given.
